ppe_compliance_ontology_limitation.why_not_semantically_exact: PPE_ISSUE (aliases 'ppe issue'/'ppe non compliance') denotes a specific negative finding/instance of non-compliance. 'PPE Compliance' is the source sheet's own Observation Category label -- a broad topic covering PPE-related observations generally, not exclusively non-compliant ones. Approving PPE_ISSUE would silently assume all 117 records were negative findings, an approximate-category substitution this milestone explicitly forbids.
ppe_compliance_ontology_limitation.action_taken: Left REJECTED/quarantined; not represented safely by the current ontology. No new canonical value invented.
ppe_compliance_ontology_limitation.recommendation: A future, deliberate ontology-review milestone could add a dedicated 'PPE compliance topic/category' Observation-subtype value distinct from PPE_ISSUE -- out of this milestone's explicit scope.

compound_event_subtype_mechanism.why_needed: The real workbook's Incident sheet (app/validation/real_dataset_loader.py) has no subtype-bearing column at all -- only event_type is populated for Incident-sheet rows. Without a compound target, an event_type-only decision for NearMiss/PropertyDamage/VehicleAccident could only ever resolve event_type, collapsing all three (plus the already-MAPPED Injury term) into an indistinguishable event_type=INCIDENT.
compound_event_subtype_mechanism.how_it_works: An event_type-domain TerminologyMappingDecision may declare provenance['target_event_subtype'], validated by _valid_compound_subtype_for() before approval. Applied by the adapter/reprocessing service ONLY when the record's own raw event_subtype is empty -- a genuine independent raw subtype value always takes precedence.
compound_event_subtype_mechanism.compound_validation_corrective_commit_v2: _valid_compound_subtype_for(canonical_event_type) now returns EXACTLY that event_type's own curated subtype vocabulary (_SUBTYPE_ALIASES[canonical_event_type].values()) plus a narrow, explicit, one-pair-at-a-time exception list (_COMPOUND_SUBTYPE_SIBLING_EXCEPTIONS), seeded with exactly {INCIDENT: {NEAR_MISS}} -- the one pairing an actual governed decision requires. NEVER a union with all of SafetyEventType (the prior version's bug -- it let INCIDENT+OBSERVATION, INCIDENT+PERMIT, INCIDENT+TRAINING all incorrectly validate). PROPERTY_DAMAGE and VEHICLE_INCIDENT need no exception -- both are already in INCIDENT's own curated subtype vocabulary.
compound_event_subtype_mechanism.no_migration: Rides entirely on TerminologyMappingDecision.provenance, the existing JSON column already used for version-supersession bookkeeping. The sibling-exceptions table lives in terminology_calibration_service.py (the governance/validation layer) -- terminology_mapping.py's own _SUBTYPE_ALIASES ontology table is never modified.
canonical_values_reused_not_invented: NEAR_MISS (existing SafetyEventType, reused via the explicit sibling-exception list)

architecture_limitations_discovered: A plain re-ingest can never re-trigger reclassification for content that has not changed (SafetyEventIngestionService idempotency compares the raw payload hash, not its resolution) -- reprocessing must call validate_and_normalize()/_apply() directly, not re-run ingest_batch().
training_status/maintenance_status domains have no ingestion adapter that gates classification on them -- calibration approval for those domains has nothing to unlock; reprocessing refuses them.

DataSourceAdapter.validate()/normalize() take no database session by design, so the calibration-aware adapter requires a precomputed active-mapping index rebuilt once per ingestion batch, not a live query.

The real workbook's Incident sheet provides no subtype-bearing raw column at all (prior milestone's finding) -- addressed via the compound event_type+subtype target mechanism, never by modifying the ingestion format.

SIE's OBSERVATION canonical subtype vocabulary has no dedicated value for the broader 'PPE compliance' topic distinct from the narrower PPE_ISSUE (prior milestone's finding) -- see ppe_compliance_ontology_limitation.

A governed decision persisted only in an ephemeral database is not durable by default (corrective-commit finding) -- fixed by the decision artifact; the general pattern (a governed decision needs an explicit, durable, version-controlled artifact to outlive the session that made it) generalizes to any future governed-decision mechanism.

A blanket union with an entire enum is a materially weaker guarantee than 'a genuine subtype of this specific event_type', even though both avoid inventing a brand-new canonical string (corrective-commit finding) -- fixed via a narrow, explicit, one-pair-at-a-time exception list instead of a type-system-wide union.
recommendations_for_next_milestone: A deliberate ontology-review milestone to decide whether OBSERVATION should gain a dedicated 'PPE compliance topic' canonical value, and whether any of the other 14 rejected terms warrant a genuinely new canonical value.
A minimal API router (app/api/v1/terminology_calibration.py) so a real reviewer can drive the lifecycle from the product UI rather than a script.
The 437 records for the 15 rejected terms remain quarantined by design -- no further action expected unless a future ontology-review milestone changes the underlying vocabulary.

A real deployment wanting the same 13-record reprocessing outcome must itself apply the decision artifact and then separately, deliberately call reprocess_quarantined_records() against its own real quarantined records -- neither step is automatic and neither was performed against real data by this corrective commit.
